title: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction: What 2,848 Billed Runs Reveal About Prompt-Cache Economics in Coding Agents (Weinberger, Hozez)
finding: Provider-billed cost; cache write 44.3%+read 35.4%+output 10.4%+uncached 1.3%+unattributed 8.7% of bill; -38% tool-output tokens gave +6.8% paired cost (CI +2.8 to +11.3); token vs cost change r=0.15; task-clustered bootstrap, ICC 0.37-0.55 so Kish n~38-45; reconstruction residual 8.7% (thinking charges); recommends reporting cache-creation/read/uncached/generated, turns, cost per success, CI with clustering unit; recommends labelling cache by source (system, tool schemas, tool output)
key_limitation: Claude Code only (Anthropic explicit cache, 1.25x write), single harness; 5-min TTL carryover between arms cannot be excluded; not preregistered; no non-inferiority margin; does not test tool-definition exposure

title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? (Bai et al.)
finding: 8 LLMs OpenHands SWE-bench Verified, 4 runs per problem; input not output drives cost even with caching; Sonnet-4.5 cache reads dominate tokens and dollars in every phase; higher tokens not higher accuracy (peaks at intermediate cost); same task cost varies (abstract: up to 30x tokens; body: avg most expensive run ~2x cheapest - internally inconsistent per summarizer); models underpredict own cost
key_limitation: coding agent not tool-heavy API agent; no tool-definition manipulation; inconsistent variance numbers across abstract/body

title: Don't Break the Cache: Evaluation of Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks (Lumer et al.)
finding: 500+ sessions DeepResearch Bench, OpenAI/Anthropic/Google; caching cut cost 27.8-80% (abstract 41-80%) and TTFT; naive full-context caching can increase latency; changing tool set invalidates cached prefix (stated, untested); 40 sessions/condition, t-tests, 24h separation between conditions to expire TTL
key_limitation: 10k-token system prompt; tool defs position untested; internal inconsistencies in ranges; no CIs; no output-token inclusion stated; one benchmark

title: AI Agents That Matter (Kapoor et al.)
finding: Report dollar cost not proxies; Pareto frontier of accuracy vs cost; 5 runs, Student-t 95% CI; error bars rare; variable cost dominates at scale; costs change over time (price volatility); simple baselines beat complex agents
key_limitation: no caching discussion; HumanEval/HotPotQA era; 2024 pricing

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard (Kapoor et al.), ICLR 2026
finding: 21,730 rollouts, 9 models x 9 benchmarks, ~$40k; per-token prices fixed at 2025-09-24; 21 of 36 combos higher reasoning effort gives equal or lower accuracy; Pareto by tokens vs by dollars give very different pictures; model identity may change on aggregators (OpenRouter quantizations); secondary summary says incomplete cost accounting for caching is a stated limitation (not verified in primary text I read)
key_limitation: computed cost from price table, not invoiced; caching treatment not found in portion read; repeat counts per config not stated

title: Adding Error Bars to Evals (Miller, Anthropic)
finding: Clustered SE can be >3x naive; recommends paired question-level differences (reduces variance when correlated); power formula; resampling K times reduces only conditional variance (cap 2/3 in example); advises against lowering temperature to cut variance
key_limitation: asymptotic CLT; assumes independent clusters; examples mostly fictional; designed for ~1000-question evals

title: On Randomness in Agentic Evals (Bjarnason, Silva, Monperrus), ICLR 2026
finding: 60,000 SWE-bench Verified trajectories, 10 runs per config; single-run pass@1 spans 2.2-6.0 pts, SD up to ~1.8 pts even at temp 0; 2-pt effect needs ~9 runs, 1-pt needs ~36 (sigma 1.5, 80% power); temp 0 delays but does not remove divergence; pass@k vs pass^k gaps large
key_limitation: SWE-bench, append-only context, 3 open models, per-run cost variance not reported

title: Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals With Fewer Than a Few Hundred Datapoints (Bowyer et al.), ICML 2025
finding: CLT intervals underestimate uncertainty on small benchmarks; bootstrap also performs poorly; Bayesian or exact-style intervals recommended; code bayes_evals
key_limitation: about accuracy proportions, not cost; I did not read full paper

title: On cost-per-task of reduction tools: Quesma 'Does RTK make AI coding cheaper?'
finding: 1,740 Terminal-Bench 2.1 attempts, 5 runs per task per arm, two harnesses; tool-output chars -9% but prompt tokens +9%; cache reads 94-98% of input tokens but only 26-30% of bill; output (incl reasoning) ~56% of DeepSeek cost; Fable saving came from one task; +17% DeepSeek; the tool's own 'tokens saved' counter claims 89%
key_limitation: blog not peer reviewed; billing basis (billed vs computed) not stated; one tool

title: Agentic AI Workload Characteristics (Yuan et al.), IISWC 2026
finding: ReAct agents on 5 benchmarks with Gemma/Qwen: with effective context caching most input tokens are reused across turns; execution becomes decode-dominated
key_limitation: abstract only; serving-side not billing

title: CacheRouter
finding: Keeps a small fixed core toolset in main prefix, routes long-tail tools via sub-model; 91-95% cache hit, input cost 8-12% of no-cache under DeepSeek pricing
key_limitation: 55 queries + one 30-turn dialogue; no accuracy reported in abstract; only no-cache baseline

title: Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs (Cai et al.), NeurIPS 2025
finding: Software-only detection of substituted/quantized models is unreliable; log-prob tests undermined by inference nondeterminism
key_limitation: no evidence of actual widespread substitution; threat-model paper

title: OpenRouter 'Not pinning your provider might invalidate your research' (Khoriaty, LessWrong) incl. 'The Silent Hyperparameter' pointer
finding: Providers of same fp8 model gave 'drastically different' capability in one reanalysis; routing logs show mixed providers in one config; recommends pin provider, allow_fallbacks false, record provider per response
key_limitation: secondhand, partly LLM-assisted; author acknowledges errors

title: The Silent Hyperparameter: inference backends and LLM reproducibility (Pape et al.), NeurIPS 2026
finding: Backend alone shifts benchmark scores by up to 16.6 pts at fixed weights/decoding/hardware; prefix caching and CUDA graphs among causes; report backend+version
key_limitation: abstract only; 4B-30B models, GSM8K-type tasks

title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference (Thinking Machines)
finding: Temp-0 nondeterminism mainly from non-batch-invariant kernels, depends on server load; 1000 samples gave 80 unique completions; batch-invariant kernels gave identical
key_limitation: single model, vendor blog

title: OpenRouter Exacto / Provider variance announcement
finding: OpenRouter says provider tool-call accuracy varies; parsers more common cause than quantization; Exacto routing improved Tau2/LiveMCP 10-20%
key_limitation: vendor self-report; not independently verified

title: OpenRouter usage accounting docs
finding: Returns cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost; upstream_inference_cost only for BYOK; doc does not say if cost is computed or invoiced
key_limitation: ambiguity on computed-vs-invoiced

title: Anthropic prompt caching docs
finding: Order tools->system->messages; tool-definition change invalidates all three; write 1.25x (5 min) / 2x (1 h); read 0.1x (some models 0.025-0.05x); hits not guaranteed (concurrent requests, 20-block lookback, TTL)
key_limitation: Anthropic-specific; our models use other caching schemes

title: Invisible Tokens, Visible Bills (Sun et al.) / CoIn
finding: Hidden reasoning tokens can exceed visible answer tokens by >10x; billing inflation vectors; user-side audit proposals (CoIn up to 94.7% detection of count inflation)
key_limitation: snippet-level; position paper

title: Cost-of-Pass (Erol et al.), ICLR 2026
finding: Expected cost per correct solution as metric; inference-time techniques often not worth cost
key_limitation: not opened; per-token price based

title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks (ABC)
finding: 10 benchmarks audited; 7 outcome-validity flaws, 7 task-validity issues; all 10 incomplete reporting; flaws shift measured performance up to 100% relative
key_limitation: not opened; AppWorld not confirmed among benchmarks

title: tau-bench (Yao et al.)
finding: pass^k reliability; gpt-4o pass^8 <25% in retail
key_limitation: abstract only

title: Pixis 'LLM inference cost' blog (quadratic formula)
finding: N*P + t*N(N-1)/2 input growth under no-cache accounting; 20K prefix 1.5K per step 40 steps ~1.97M in vs 24K out
key_limitation: blog, no-cache arithmetic; with caching rates the weights change
